parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the Python argparse float option, canonicaljson float encoding, bytes-style printed output, exact CLI behavior, ESM .mjs modules, local or builtin imports only, and the no-JSON.stringify constraint.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It used a two-wave plan: four subagents each owned one library file, then a fifth integration subagent owned the entry point and end-to-end verification, with the parent reserving final review and closure.
parallel.implementation: The children wrote pyfloat.mjs, pybytes.mjs, canonicaljson.mjs, and argparse.mjs at the output root; the integration child wrote test3.mjs and made a one-line help-indent correction in argparse.mjs after differential testing.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The integration child read the four modules, imported them with .mjs suffixes, wired parseArgs to encodeCanonicalJson and pyBytesRepr, reported the touched files, and the parent spot-checked final output before delivery.
parallel.verification: Module-level tests covered each child assignment; integration then ran 28 fixed executable comparisons, 200 randomized differentials, a constraint grep, and parent spot checks. The official evaluator later passed 148/148.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished requirement remains in the completed official record; the only observed interim mismatch was argparse help indentation, corrected before final handoff.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same argparse, float repr, canonicaljson bytes output, ESM .mjs, no dependency, no Python embedding, and no JSON.stringify requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It kept all work in one actor, explored executable behavior first, then wrote a lib-based modular implementation plus a root test3.mjs entry point without delegation.
serial.implementation: It produced lib/pyFloat.mjs, lib/pyRepr.mjs, lib/canonicalJson.mjs, lib/argparse.mjs, and test3.mjs, including a broader hand-written canonical JSON implementation than strictly needed for numeric input.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The single actor controlled all interfaces locally, imported the lib modules from test3.mjs, observed and cleaned a local argparse usage helper detail, then delivered a complete file list.
serial.verification: It ran sample outputs, 57 differential tests, help and error formatting checks, then a detached 300-case fuzz comparison whose completion log ended with fuzz OK. The official evaluator later passed 148/148.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or evaluator-visible incorrect behavior remains in the completed official record; the final response reports all fixed, random, help, and error checks passing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required Python argparse float behavior, canonical JSON float representation, bytes-style printed output, ESM .mjs modules, zero dependencies, and no JSON.stringify.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same task obligations and probed the executable for float formatting, argparse edge cases, non-finite errors, help, and invalid arguments.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement gap exists. Parallel encoded the requirements into child-specific briefs, while serial carried the same requirements in one actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split ownership by file: pyfloat, pybytes, canonicaljson, argparse, and then a separate integration agent for test3.mjs and verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a single owner for exploration, all library modules, the entry file, and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel distributed implementation across child-owned root files and then rejoined through an integration agent; serial avoided coordination boundaries by keeping ownership local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs specified file ownership, exports, imports, and verification obligations, and child handoffs reported interfaces and test results before integration.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept interface knowledge in one local context and implemented the hierarchy with direct local imports under lib.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more interface boundaries, but they were explicit and consumed; serial had fewer boundaries because one actor controlled all contracts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented narrow task-specific root modules: Python float helpers, bytes repr, number-only canonicaljson, argparse, and a root entry point.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a lib directory with pyFloat, pyRepr, canonicalJson, argparse, and test3.mjs, including more general canonical JSON support beyond number input.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented the required behavior, but parallel used narrower components and serial used a broader library-style implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All four library children completed, the parent received the aggregate result, then the integration child completed and returned verification details.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No child lifecycle exists in serial; the main actor progressed from exploration through implementation, detached fuzz verification, consumed the completion notification, and finalized.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child result collection and a second delegated integration lifecycle; serial had only local task and background process completion handling.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel agents wrote separate assigned root files in the shared output directory; the later integration agent wrote test3.mjs and edited one completed helper file after finding a genuine mismatch.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all files itself under a lib hierarchy plus the root entry point, so shared-state provenance stayed within one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared-workspace coordination but no collision or unresolved provenance problem; serial avoided concurrent writes by construction.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel combined child unit checks, integration executable comparisons, 200 randomized cases, a constraints grep, a parent spot check, and official evaluator success.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran sample checks, 57 differential cases, help/error checks, a 300-case fuzz run, and official evaluator success.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had strong acceptance evidence. Serial's self-test set was larger; parallel still covered the key fixed cases, randomized behavior, constraints, and official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used more requests, tool calls, and tokens because of five subagents, but it did not time out and closed with a parent spot-check after child verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used fewer requests and no subagents, ran a detached fuzz task to completion, and closed after reading the completion output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel paid coordination overhead but did not suffer budget displacement; serial was simpler and slightly faster while both remained comfortably within the cell budget.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations passed all 148 tests, so there is no discordant outcome to explain. The parallel run differed by delegating module construction and integration to subagents, while the serial run kept all implementation and testing in one actor. The visible parallel coordination produced overhead and one later helper edit, but the integration pass consumed child results, corrected the mismatch, verified against the executable, and delivered a passing artifact.
parallel_contributors: Four child-owned library modules were completed and returned before the integration child wrote the entry point.
The integration child corrected an argparse help-indent mismatch and reran verification before the parent closed.
serial_contributors: The serial actor maintained all interface decisions in one context and wrote a lib-based implementation.
The serial actor completed fixed differential tests and a 300-case fuzz run before final delivery.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used narrow number-only canonicaljson behavior, while serial implemented a broader canonical JSON module; both satisfied the numeric task.
Parallel placed library modules at the output root, while serial placed them under lib; both used valid ESM imports and delivered test3.mjs.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome difference; supported process contrast only.

candidates.reason: Implementation had explicit owners: four library modules were assigned through AgentSwarm and the entry point was assigned to the integration child.
Integration was explicitly delegated to agent-4 after the library handoffs, and agent-4 read modules, wrote test3.mjs, fixed argparse, and verified end to end.
The final assembly and required entry file were assigned to agent-4, which created test3.mjs and reported the final artifact set.
The parent owned the overall flow from probing to module delegation, integration delegation, final spot check, and closure; no transition was left ownerless.
The parent did probe executable behavior before delegation, but the probes were short, informed the child briefs, and did not block productive work into an adverse delay window.

The parent performed limited serial exploration, then parallel implementation completed and was verified; no later implementation or integration stage was deadline-constrained by an investigation phase.
The indispensable path had a dedicated integration child and a parent final check; no required implementation, integration, or correction work was starved of capacity.
The four-way module fan-out plus one integration child increased overhead, but all children completed, the run did not time out, and verification and official evaluation succeeded.
No single child received an overbroad unfinished assignment; each scoped module or integration task returned a concrete result, and the only discovered bug was fixed by the integration child.
The child prompts carried the global constraints plus file-specific behavior and verification duties, and the children followed those briefs well enough for integration and official success.

Delegations specified filenames and exports, such as canonicaljson importing pyFloatRepr from pyfloat.mjs and the entry importing the four modules, so no incompatible independently produced interface remained.
No known finding or constraint disappeared in transfer; the aggregate swarm result reached the parent and the integration child received the file and interface facts needed to complete.
The swarm handoff was long, but the parent reduced it by launching an integration agent that read the modules and completed verification; no needed result was left unconsumed.
No child or parent acted on a superseded state; the integration child observed the current module files, found the argparse help state, edited it, and retested.
The completed child reports did not contain incompatible contracts needing adjudication; integration found only one concrete implementation mismatch and corrected it.
The parent did not accept the work on file existence alone; it had the integration child verification report and then ran an independent spot check before final response.
No replacement or retry child repeated prior work without inherited findings; the integration child was a new planned stage, not a checkpoint-free retry.

candidates.reason: No executed child was cancelled or interrupted before a needed result; all five child agents reached completed handoffs.
A usable final candidate was not left unpromoted; test3.mjs was written by the integration child, verified, spot-checked, and included in artifact validation.
The integration child edited argparse.mjs only after a differential mismatch and then reran the fixed-case and randomized verification before reporting success.
The delegated library implementations were present in the shared output and were read, imported, and verified by the integration child, so no completed implementation was left unjoined.
The verifier/integration child returned concrete fixed-test, random-test, and constraint-check results to the parent before closure.
No required child failed or was cancelled; the only identified defect was an argparse help-indent mismatch that the integration child took over and fixed.
The parent consumed the completed swarm result by delegating integration with those modules and consumed the integration result before final spot-checking.
The parent did not wait to timeout or near deadline without inspection; after children returned, it launched integration and then performed a final spot check.
Agents wrote different assigned files, but the scopes were complementary modules with explicit imports and no competing design that required unresolved reconciliation.
Only one child initially owned argparse.mjs; the later one-line edit occurred after module completion during integration, not as concurrent same-file editing.
No live actor replaced or wholesale rewrote another actor's non-entry source; the observed argparse change was a targeted post-handoff bug fix.
The required entry point test3.mjs was created by the integration child and was not overwritten while another agent owned or used it.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replacing multiple current outputs or invalidating another agent's final-tree work.
Although children shared /output, each had a separate file owner and no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem resulted.
Scratch test files remained under /tmp and were used only by their owning checks; no generated artifact or cache from one actor contaminated another actor's reference environment.
